Pusztadobos Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kossuth utca 10, Hungary

Not demolished. Established in 1863, this cemetery served a small community — never more than 93 people, its 1880 peak — that joined the Orthodox stream after Hungarian Jewry's 1869 Congress split. In mid-April 1944, residents were forced from their homes, carted to the Kisvárda Ghetto, and crowded into just two rooms before deportation to Auschwitz in May; only 14 survivors returned afterward, and none stayed to revive the community. Note: this record appears to duplicate another entry in this collection, 'Pustadobos Jewish Cemetery' (a likely typo of this town's name), which shares the same coordinates and physical description but contains only placeholder text in place of genuine history.
